label: rare: step right after an i late in the original phase / at <DEL> (sequences rich in i, j, t)
explanation: Extremely sparse (0.005% of steps). Fires only in the original phase at t>=4 (64% of mass) or at the <DEL> step (36%), and never in the copy phase or at t<3. The strongest cue is that the previous input was i: 62% of activations, 22x lift. Sequences also tend to contain j and t earlier and to start with y/k/w/l. But the conjunction is very weak: prev_tok==i at t>=4 has precision 0.003, and adding first-token and seen-j/t conditions only gets precision to about 0.05 while recall falls to 0.3. This looks like a highly specific hidden-state direction with no simple token-level description. Magnitude is nearly uniform (0.1-0.19), and I found nothing that clearly modulates it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=i (+4.57), orig0=y (+3.59), orig0=k (+3.39), orig0=w (+2.98), orig2=j (+2.65), orig3=j (+2.64). Lower it: phase=2 (-2.91), prev3_tok=- (-2.68), t=3 (-2.33), in_first=0 (-1.33).
